title: Customized Covenant Creation Summary
heading: Customized Covenant Creation Summary
summary: Overview of the covenant creation procedure: start from the baseline, choose a power level, then pick Boons and Hooks and spend Build Points on resources.
quotes: Starting from the baseline below, choose a power level

title: Covenant Baseline
heading: Baseline
summary: Describes what a default covenant already has before any Boons, Hooks or resources are bought: its building, aura, defenses, income, labs and covenfolk.
quotes: The covenant has a Living Conditions modifier of +1 for magi and 0 for everybody else.

title: Covenant Power Level and Build Points
heading: Power Level
summary: The troupe chooses one of four power levels (low, medium, high, legendary), which sets the Build Points, the maximum level of lab texts and enchanted-device effects, and the minimum age of the covenant.

title: Covenant Boons and Hooks (Creation Summary)
heading: Boons and Hooks
summary: Explains that Boons improve the covenant and Hooks generate stories, with Major, Minor and Free kinds, and that Hooks supply the points that pay for Boons.
quotes: Thus, a covenant cannot start with more points of Boons than points of Hooks.

title: Covenant Resource Costs in Build Points
heading: Resources
summary: Build Point costs for buying enchanted items, extra and non-standard laboratories, laboratory texts and library books (Art and Ability summae, tractatus) at covenant creation.
quotes: 2 per five levels of effects
Extra labs: 50 each
Tractatus: Quality (Quality limit: 11)

title: Covenant Build Point Costs: Money, Specialists and Vis
heading: Money
summary: Build Point costs for starting stocks of money, for specialist covenfolk (teachers and others) and for vis sources and stocks.
quotes: Sources: 5 per pawn of vis per year
Stocks: 1 per 5 pawns of vis

title: The Covenant in Play: Gaining and Losing Boons and Hooks
heading: The Covenant in Play
summary: After play begins the covenant gets no more Build Points; resources change through the characters' actions, and gaining a Boon should bring a matching Hook while a lost Boon becomes something to win back.
quotes: If a Boon is gained, the covenant should gain a corresponding Hook

title: Tips for a Smoothly Run Covenant
heading: Some Tips for a Smoothly Run Covenant
summary: Practical advice on keeping covenant records: shared notes, delegated library, vis and finance tracking, vis tokens, an annual calendar and a covenant logbook.

title: Paying for Choices (Boon and Hook Balance, Unknown Hook)
heading: Paying for Choices
summary: Explains how Major and Minor Boons and Hooks are paid for and balanced at creation, how the Unknown Hook works, how many Hooks a troupe should take, and how Boons and Hooks change during play.
quotes: Covenants created by troupes as homes for player character magi should balance.
The Unknown Hook is a Major Hook for balancing Boons.
select no more Hooks than you are likely to use in six months of real-time play

title: Conversion from the Ars Magica Rules
heading: Conversion from the Ars Magica Rules
summary: How to convert covenants built with the core book's Boons and Hooks to this book's definitions, and what replaces the old Buildings and Fortifications Boons.

title: Major Site Boons
heading: Major Site Boons
summary: The Major Boons describing the covenant's site, such as an extra aura point in a limited area, a conscious space, a fantastic environment, immunity, a natural fortress, a regio, and time dilation or contraction.
quotes: The aura of a limited area of the covenant increases by one point.
Vis sources within the regio usually refresh in mundane time.

title: Minor Site Boons
heading: Minor Site Boons
summary: The Minor Boons for the covenant's site, including extra aura points (repeatable), difficult access, a healthy feature that helps aging rolls, immunity, a mystical portal, regio, seclusion, unnatural law, vast aura and vivid environment.
quotes: The players may take this Boon up to seven times, for a covenant in any magic aura up to ten.
Inhabitants with access to this feature have a +1 bonus on their aging rolls.

title: Major Site Hooks
heading: Major Site Hooks
summary: The Major Hooks for the covenant's site: constant mobility, a highly mutable aura, a magical disaster, a missing aura, a resident monster, a mystical road, a regio on the site, and an urban location.
quotes: If the regio is not magical, that counts as an additional Minor Hook.

title: Minor Site Hooks
heading: Minor Site Hooks
summary: The Minor Hooks for the covenant's site, such as corrupt or faerie auras, curses, haunting, a flickering or weak aura, an unhealthy environment that worsens aging rolls, and several regio variants. Several of them may be taken as the Unknown Hook.
quotes: Subtract one point from the covenant's Magic aura.
All people regularly exposed to the environmental factor suffer a –1 penalty to their Aging rolls.

title: Fortifications Free Choices (Island, Manor House, Ringwork, Small Tower)
heading: Free Choices
summary: Free (no-cost) fortification options: island, manor house, ringwork and small tower, noting which of them need the Castle Hook and how neighbouring nobles react to each.
quotes: Several of the Free Choices in this section require the Castle Hook.

title: Castle (Major Hook)
heading: Castle (Major Hook)
summary: Explains why a castle forces the covenant to deal with its neighbours, when the Castle Major Hook is required, and how ringworks, keeps and curtain walls relate to it.
quotes: A covenant with a castle must take the Castle Major Hook, unless the covenant has no mundane neighbors within ten miles.

title: Major Fortifications Boons
heading: Major Fortifications Boons
summary: The Major fortification Boons: curtain walls and mural towers (which include a keep, barbican and moat), a magical fortress, and superior engineering.
quotes: A curtain wall is a crenellated wall around a bailey.

title: Keep Alternatives for Castles with Curtain Walls
heading: Keep Alternatives for Castles with Curtain Walls
requires: Boon: Curtain Walls and Mural Towers
summary: Four alternatives to a tower or shell keep that a castle with curtain walls may choose at no extra cost: hall keep, courtyard castle, gatehouse keep and chemise.

title: Barbicans and Moats
heading: Barbicans and Moats
requires: Boon: Curtain Walls and Mural Towers
summary: Defines what a barbican and a moat are for game purposes and how a covenant obtains them, free with Curtain Walls and Mural Towers or otherwise as Edifices or Important Buildings.
quotes: A moat is a body of water at least twenty feet wide and six feet deep that surrounds the covenant.

title: Minor Fortifications Boons
heading: Minor Fortifications Boons
summary: The Minor fortification Boons: artillery, bedrock foundations, edifices, important buildings, shell keep, tower keep, a vast and labyrinthine layout and a writ of crenellation.
quotes: Edifices do not require the Castle Hook unless several of them, grouped together, form a structure as threatening as a castle.

title: Minor Fortifications Hooks
heading: Minor Fortifications Hooks
summary: The Minor fortification Hooks: a crumbling castle, outbuildings clustering around it, and wooden construction.

title: Major Resources Boon (Wealth)
heading: Major Resources Boon
summary: The Major Resources Boon upgrades one existing Typical source of income to Legendary.
quotes: One existing Typical source of income is upgraded to Legendary

title: Minor Resources Boons
heading: Minor Resources Boons
summary: Minor Boons for covenant wealth: hidden resources, a right to collect income, secondary income, a vis grant, and a lesser Wealth boon that upgrades a Typical income to Greater.
quotes: The covenant has 250 Build Points of resources that are not immediately available to the player characters.
One existing Typical source of income is upgraded to Greater

title: Major Resources Hooks
heading: Major Resources Hooks
summary: Major Hooks about the covenant's wealth: a crippling debt, an indiscreet (criminal) resource, a natural disaster that destroys the main source of wealth, and total poverty.
quotes: The yearly interest due on the debt alone amounts to about three quarters of the covenant's entire income

title: Minor Resources Hooks
heading: Minor Resources Hooks
summary: Minor Hooks about wealth: contested, dwindling, flawed and illusory resources, a moderate debt, an indiscreet resource, a natural disaster, poverty, regional produce and vis salary. Several give a concrete rate of loss or interest.
quotes: As a rule, one story means that the resource is available for five years.
The resource loses 10% of its original value per year
The yearly interest due on the debt is equal to about one quarter of the covenant's income

title: Style of Governance (Covenfolk)
heading: Style of Governance
summary: A Free Choice of how the covenfolk (not the magi) are governed: autocracy, council, democracy, faux feudalism, gerontocracy, militocracy or theocracy.
quotes: Each covenant should select one of the following styles by which the residents of the covenant are governed.

title: Residents: Paying for Background Characters
heading: Residents
summary: Residents Boons and Hooks do not affect player-character preparation, and a background character who fits several Boons only needs to be paid for once.
quotes: A background character who fulfills several roles, and could be purchased with any of several Boons, needs only to be purchased once.

title: Residents Free Choices
heading: Residents Free Choices
summary: Free Choices for the covenant's defenders: hunters or sailors, who are paid, and peasant soldiers who serve as part of their rent.
quotes: These people need payment, a penny per day, for their service

title: Crossbow Rules and Statistics
heading: Crossbows
summary: Interim rules for reloading crossbows (time depends on Strength and the winding system), a limit of one bolt per round, and a statistics table for historical and anachronistic crossbows.
quotes: A crossbow takes (5 – Strength) minutes to reload.
No character may discharge a bolt more than once per combat round.

title: Major Residents Boons
heading: Major Residents Boons
summary: Major Boons for covenant residents: heavy cavalry, magical soldiers and a tame nobleman, each with consequences for how neighbouring nobles react.

title: Minor Residents Boons
heading: Minor Residents Boons
summary: Minor Boons for residents, including cavalry, crossbowmen, veteran fighters, inhuman residents, literate or loyal covenfolk (Loyal Covenfolk sets the starting Prevailing Loyalty) and a strong community.
quotes: After calculating Base Loyalty, add sufficient loyalty points to raise the Prevailing Loyalty of the covenant to +3 (30 loyalty points total).
They receive nine pence each day, even if they are not required to fight.
They receive a penny each per day, even if they are not required to fight.

title: Major Residents Hooks
heading: Major Residents Hooks
summary: Major Hooks about residents, including Divided Loyalty (separate Prevailing Loyalty per faction) and Rebellious Covenfolk (very low starting loyalty), plus diabolic corruption, a chapter house, a school and superiors.
quotes: Actions which benefit the loyalty of one faction over the others will cause a decrease in loyalty of the other factions equal to one half of the loyalty points gained.
Subtract sufficient loyalty points to obtain a loyalty point total of –75 (a Prevailing Loyalty of –5).

title: Minor Residents Hooks
heading: Minor Residents Hooks
summary: Minor Hooks about residents, such as alienable land, dark secrets, fosterage, gender imbalance, a guild, a house church, incompetent or inhuman covenfolk, infants, spies and superiors.

title: Military Preparedness
heading: Military Preparedness
summary: Lists which Residents Boons and Free Choices describe non-player fighters, noting that player characters are built with the grog or companion rules instead.
quotes: Player characters are exceptions to these general descriptions, and are created using the grog or companion rules.

title: Major External Relations Boons
heading: Major External Relations Boons
summary: Major Boons for the covenant's dealings with outsiders, such as autocephalous status, a dedicated covenant, an exceptional book, favors owed, a hedge tradition, high Prestige and a powerful ally.
quotes: The book's (level + quality) = 35, with a maximum quality of 25 and a maximum Art level of 20.
The covenant has a Reputation score of 9.

title: Minor External Relations Boons
heading: Minor External Relations Boons
summary: Minor Boons for the covenant's dealings with outsiders: benefice, a felicitous tribunal, informants, a local ally, minor Prestige, promised favors and being ungoverned.
quotes: The covenant has a Reputation score of 3.

title: Major External Relations Hooks
heading: Major External Relations Hooks
summary: Major Hooks about outsiders: being beholden, a center of excellence, hosting Order ceremonies, a rival hedge tradition, Hermetic services, mundane politics, a rival, a tribunal border and a war zone.

title: Minor External Relations Hooks
heading: Minor External Relations Hooks
summary: Minor Hooks about outsiders, such as an ancestral error, a centralized kingdom, church territories, favors owed, Hermetic politics, infamy, a public vis source, slavery and an unsafe route that Redcaps avoid.
quotes: When the saga begins, the covenant owes favors to three other covenants, but is owed three favors as well.

title: Major Surroundings Boons
heading: Major Surroundings Boons
summary: Major Boons for the covenant's surroundings: a defensive environment, tithing miracles and mystical allies.

title: Minor Surroundings Boons
heading: Minor Surroundings Boons
summary: Minor Boons for the surroundings: a chase (managed royal forest), hidden ways and a minority community.

title: Major Surroundings Hooks
heading: Major Surroundings Hooks
summary: Major Hooks for the surroundings, such as a nearby city, demonic interest, an enclosed covenant, a faerie landlord, a meddlesome saint, a monster, pagans, a pilgrimage site, a ruined covenant and a seat of power.

title: Minor Surroundings Hooks
heading: Minor Surroundings Hooks
summary: Minor Hooks for the surroundings, such as death prophecies, a faerie court, a fated feat, a festival, a ford, guardians, heretics, a legendary or massacre site, a monastery, a protectorate, sanctuary and an ungarrisoned castle.

title: Covenant Situations (Prebuilt Boon and Hook Packages)
heading: Covenant Situations
summary: A set of ready-made covenant packages (such as Autumn Power, Devoted, Expedition, Hermetic Market, Struggling, Urban and Worshipful), each a balanced list of Boons, Hooks and Free Choices that a troupe can adopt and tailor.
quotes: Each covenant situation described below is a package of Boons and Hooks that balance.

title: Table of Boons and Hooks
heading: Table of Boons and Hooks
summary: Quick-reference table listing every Boon, Free Choice and Hook with its category (Site, Buildings, Resources, Residents, External, Surroundings), whether it is Major or Minor, and any prerequisite such as the Castle Hook. Bold and italic entries mark low- and high-fantasy suitability.
quotes: Entries in **bold** are particularly suited to low fantasy campaigns.

title: Forms of Governance
heading: Forms of Governance
summary: Describes the five basic ways a covenant can be governed (democracy, autocracy, hierarchy, bureaucracy, anarchy), who each suits, and how the styles can be combined.
quotes: There are five basic systems by which covenants may be governed

title: Membership of a Covenant
heading: Membership of a Covenant
summary: Normally only magi are covenant members; extending membership to non-magi needs a procedure in the charter, and such members are treated as having the same rights and duties as at least some magi.

title: Leadership and Offices
heading: Leadership
summary: How covenant leaders are chosen or removed, why a covenant benefits from appointed officers for the library, vis, money and similar duties, and Latin titles for leaders and offices.
quotes: One very effective system is to give the casting vote (which breaks ties) to the officer under whose purview a proposal falls.

title: Boons, Hooks, and Governance Styles
heading: Boons, Hooks, and Governance Styles
summary: A table suggesting which Boons, Free Choices and Hooks suit each style of governance; none of the styles requires any particular Boon or Hook.
quotes: None of the styles of governance in themselves require any specific Boons or Hooks.

title: The Council Meeting
heading: The Council Meeting
summary: Covers regular and extraordinary council meetings: scheduling by season or quarter day, what is decided there, and the use of a quorum so a single magus cannot decide for the whole covenant.
quotes: A quorum equal to more than half of the covenant's members is often considered reasonable.

title: The Charter of Covenant
heading: The Charter of Covenant
summary: Explains the Oath of Covenant and the written Charter of Covenant with its bylaws, and notes that a charter notarized by a Quaesitor becomes enforceable as part of a Tribunal's Peripheral Code.
quotes: If a charter has been notarized by a Quaesitor it is legally enforceable as part of the Tribunal's Peripheral Code.

title: Charter Section: Membership
heading: Membership
summary: The charter lists members and requirements for joining (usually Order membership and a council vote), and may define levels of membership or a period of servitude before full privileges.

title: Charter Section: Method of Governance (Voting)
heading: Method of Governance
summary: The charter sets out leadership, offices, how meetings and decisions work, who votes, how ties are broken (casting vote, extra vote, status quo or certamen) and how the charter may be changed.
quotes: The matter of breaking tied votes should also be addressed.

title: The Charter of Arae Flaviae
heading: The Charter of Arae Flaviae
summary: A model democratic charter used by many young covenants; a Quaesitor's ratification is automatic if it is adopted without alteration. A blank copy is in the Appendix.
quotes: Ratification of a charter by a Quaesitor (where this is mandatory, see below) is automatic if a covenant uses the Charter of Arae Flaviae without alteration.

title: Examples of Vote-Taking
heading: Examples of Vote-Taking
summary: Menu of options for running council votes: criteria for a legal meeting, methods of casting and allocating votes, ways to adjudicate a result (majority by vote, magus or member, threshold, unanimity) and types of voting.
quotes: Majority by Member: As above, but more than half of the magi who are members of the covenant must vote aye for the motion to be carried

title: Charter Section: Covenant Resources
heading: Covenant Resources
summary: The charter should list what the covenant owns, to separate it from members' personal property; the text lists the kinds of resources a covenant may hold.

title: Charter Section: Member Rights
heading: Member Rights
summary: How a charter divides covenant resources among members: basic food, shelter and laboratory, library and item access, vis sharing (and its link to the Vis Salary and Vis Grant options), money, and rewards for work done for the covenant.
quotes: Most charters allow magi to keep whatever vis they find, unless it proves to be a renewable source, in which case it belongs to the covenant.

title: Charter Section: Member Obligations
heading: Member Obligations
summary: The duties a charter places on members, such as safeguarding resources, harvesting vis and collecting income, often falling on the younger magi, plus any ad hoc obligations.

title: Example of a Complex Method of Governance
heading: Example of a Complex Method of Governance
summary: A worked example of a council with a disceptator, quorum, categories of issue and different voting thresholds for each.
quotes: Issues of Significance require a Majority by Member to be passed

title: The Carrot and the Stick (Standard Shares and Services)
heading: The Carrot and the Stick
summary: A sample charter rule that ties each magus's annual share of covenant vis to performing Standard Services (and optional Additional Services) for the covenant.
quotes: A magus may earn up to one extra share per year by performing an Additional Service equivalent to a Standard Service.

title: Obligations and the Code of Hermes
heading: Obligations and the Code of Hermes
summary: Explains how heavy covenant obligations interact with the Oath of Hermes ban on depriving a magus of magical power, and why a covenant may not change obligations against a magus's will.
quotes: the covenant cannot alter the obligation imposed on any magus against his will without committing a High Crime

title: Censure
heading: Censure
summary: How a covenant may punish a member who breaks the charter, through expulsion or by withholding commonly held privileges, and why denying a magus his own property or laboratory breaches the Oath of Hermes.
quotes: Expulsion from the covenant is the most serious punishment a covenant can inflict.

title: The Official Seal (Quaesitorial Ratification of a Charter)
heading: The Official Seal
summary: Some Tribunals require a charter to be approved by the Quaesitores, who may add it to the Peripheral Code; a Quaesitor can only demand changes where the charter breaks the Oath of Hermes or the Peripheral Code.
quotes: No Quaesitor can dictate the contents of a charter

title: Prevailing Loyalty
heading: Prevailing Loyalty
summary: Introduces Prevailing Loyalty, a covenant-wide measure of how loyal and well-motivated its members are, on the same scale as Personality Traits.
quotes: It is expressed as a positive or negative number on the same general scale as Personality Traits.

title: Prevailing Loyalty and Individual Loyalty
heading: Prevailing Loyalty and Individual Loyalty
summary: How an individual's Loyal to Covenant Trait relates to the covenant's Prevailing Loyalty, including how far it may deviate, and the table of Gift modifiers to Base Loyalty.
quotes: can vary by up to three points either way from the average Prevailing Loyalty of the covenant
| The Gift | –30 |
| The Blatant Gift | –105 |

title: Calculating Prevailing Loyalty (Base Loyalty)
heading: Calculating Prevailing Loyalty
summary: Procedure for finding a covenant's Prevailing Loyalty: average the magi's Gift modifiers to get Base Loyalty, add situational loyalty points, then convert the total using the Abilities: To Buy column of the Advancement Table.
quotes: Base Loyalty: Total of Gift Modifiers / Number of Magi
converting negative loyalty points into a negative Prevailing Loyalty

title: Modifying Loyalty Due to Covenant Situation
heading: Modifying Loyalty Due to Covenant Situation
summary: Loyalty points come from equipment, wages, living conditions and from up to three specialists (turb captain, steward, chamberlain) who manage the covenfolk; modifiers that affect only part of the covenfolk are scaled down in proportion.
quotes: Magi can employ up to three specialists who deal with the covenfolk on their behalf, rather than dealing with them directly.
A single individual may perform up to two of these tasks

title: Green Covenants (Loyalty)
heading: Green Covenants
summary: In a new covenant, or with newly recruited covenfolk, the Loyal to Covenant Trait is unlikely to exceed zero because the covenfolk distrust the Gifted until familiarity builds.

title: Established Covenants (Loyalty)
heading: Established Covenants
summary: Older covenants have usually gained enough Familiarity points for a Prevailing Loyalty of zero; large influxes of new covenfolk dilute this, and a new magus lowers Base Loyalty.
quotes: An established covenant usually has sufficient loyalty points through Familiarity (see below) to give them a Prevailing Loyalty of zero.

title: Sample Prevailing Loyalty Scores
heading: Sample Prevailing Loyalty Scores
summary: Describes how covenfolk behave at Prevailing Loyalty scores from -6 (on the verge of revolt, halved productivity) through 0 (content) to +6 (extraordinary devotion).
quotes: Productivity (in terms of cost-saving measures and income which rely upon covenfolk; see Chapter 5: Wealth and Poverty) of the covenant is halved due to desertion and rebellion.

title: Decreasing Loyalty Due to Actions and Events
heading: Decreasing Loyalty Due to Actions and Events
summary: Introduces the five categories of loyalty loss: attitude, punishments, wounds, local events and reputation.
quotes: five categories of Loyalty Point loss: attitude, punishments, wounds, local events, and reputations

title: Attitude (Loyalty Penalties)
heading: Attitude
summary: Extreme attitudes of the magi toward the covenfolk cost loyalty points; the penalty applies per offending magus and only the most severe penalty counts for each magus.
quotes: Only the most severe penalty applies.

title: Prevailing Loyalty with Non-magus Members
heading: Prevailing Loyalty with Non-magus Members
requires: Non-magus members with real votes on the ruling council
summary: Unmagical council members count as zero points in the Base Loyalty average, raising it, but only if their votes are equal to those of Gifted members.
quotes: Each unGifted member of the Council contributes zero points to the calculation of Base Loyalty

title: Prevailing Loyalty Example
heading: Prevailing Loyalty Example
summary: Worked example calculating Base Loyalty and Prevailing Loyalty for a covenant of six magi with a turb captain and an autocrat.
quotes: Thus, the covenant has a Base Loyalty of –38 (–225 / 6).

title: Situational Modifiers to Loyalty (Living Conditions, Equipment, Money, Specialists)
heading: Situational Modifiers to Loyalty
summary: Tables of loyalty points gained or lost for the covenfolk's living conditions, equipment, salary and pension, and for the specialists (turb captain, steward, chamberlain) who manage them.
quotes: | Covenant grants a standard salary (standard Wages) | 0 |
| Turb Captain | + (Prs + Leadership) |

title: Example Loyalty Point Penalties
heading: Example Loyalty Point Penalties
summary: Table of loyalty point penalties from -1 to -15 for magi's Attitude, Punishment, Wounds dealt to covenfolk and Local Events, with notes on what each Attitude entry means.
quotes: | –1 | Rudeness | Minor Humiliation | Superficial | Minor Hardship |

title: Punishment (Loyalty Penalties)
heading: Punishment
summary: A magus ordering physical punishment of a resident causes a loyalty penalty, adjusted by the victim's Reputation and only applying to unjust punishment when Prevailing Loyalty is positive.
quotes: If dearly loved, add the Reputation to the penalty

title: Wounds (Loyalty Penalties)
heading: Wounds
summary: Wounds a magus deals to covenfolk cost loyalty points, one category worse if inflicted by magic, halved for accidental wounds to grogs defending the covenant, and increased by the Reputation of a dead character.
quotes: If the wound is inflicted by magic, it is treated as one category more severe.

title: Local Events (Loyalty Penalties)
heading: Local Events
summary: Hardships and disasters in the area lower morale even when the magi are not at fault, and the penalty persists unless the magi help resolve the event.

title: Example of the Effects on Loyalty of Changing Membership
heading: Example of the Effects on Loyalty of Changing Membership
summary: Worked example of how recruiting more covenfolk dilutes Familiarity points, and how adding a magus with the Blatant Gift changes Base Loyalty.
quotes: If the number of covenfolk is doubled through recruitment, the 38 loyalty points from familiarity are diluted by one-half to 19

title: Reputation (Loyalty Loss)
heading: Reputation
summary: A bad Reputation known to the covenfolk costs the covenant loyalty points for each point of that Reputation.
quotes: The covenant loses five Loyalty Points for every point of each such Reputation.

title: Increasing Loyalty Due to Actions and Events
heading: Increasing Loyalty Due to Actions and Events
summary: Introduces the five ways to gain loyalty points: familiarity, altruism, rewards, local events and reputation.

title: Familiarity (Loyalty Gain)
heading: Familiarity
summary: Covenfolk grow used to the home covenant's magi, so the covenant gains loyalty points each year up to the amount that offsets its negative Base Loyalty.
quotes: For every year that a covenant exists it gains two loyalty points.

title: Altruism (Loyalty Gain)
heading: Altruism
summary: Magi who personally help covenfolk, for example by assisting in healing or taking a wound for them, earn loyalty points equal to the matching penalty, with conspicuous magic raising the gain a level.
quotes: Conspicuous use of magic in such altruistic acts increases the bonus to the next level.

title: Rewards (Loyalty Gain)
heading: Rewards
summary: Celebrations and a regular cycle of feast days earn the covenant loyalty points, at a cost to its wealth.
quotes: A one-off celebration after a notable event earns one Loyalty Point

title: Local Events (Loyalty Gain)
heading: Local Events
summary: Good fortune only raises loyalty if the magi clearly caused it; then the bonus equals the penalty that the same event would have caused.

title: Reputation (Loyalty Gain)
heading: Reputation
summary: A good local Reputation known to the covenfolk gives loyalty points for each point of Reputation.
quotes: then five loyalty points are gained for every point of the Reputation.

title: Loyalty and Mentem Magic
heading: Loyalty and Mentem Magic
summary: Creo and Rego Mentem spells can create devotion, cure disloyalty or force obedience, but to change Prevailing Loyalty they must be powerful and regularly used, which causes Warping.

title: Loyalty Versus Discipline (Prevailing Discipline)
heading: Loyalty Versus Discipline
summary: Optional rule that tracks Prevailing Discipline like Prevailing Loyalty, so that harsh punishment can raise discipline while lowering loyalty and indulgence does the reverse.
quotes: Maintaining Prevailing Discipline requires all specialists managing the covenfolk to use Leadership rather than their Profession Ability to maintain order.

title: Stories Caused by Prevailing Loyalty
heading: Stories Caused by Prevailing Loyalty
summary: A low Prevailing Loyalty produces periodic crises and acts like a Hook that is resolved by stories adding loyalty points.
quotes: A covenant with a Prevailing Loyalty score of –3 or less is prone to periodic crises of faithfulness

title: Covenfolk: Characters Versus Purchased Specialists
heading: Chapter Four: Covenfolk
summary: Covenfolk can be bought as specialists with Build Points, which gives them Abilities but no character sheet, or created as grogs or companions, which costs no Build Points; the chapter recommends real characters and suits slow and medium saga speeds best.
quotes: Characters created as grogs or companions, however, need not be paid for with Build Points.

title: Troupe Styles and Covenfolk
heading: Troupe Styles and Covenfolk
summary: Shows how covenfolk fit the Alternative Characters and Pooled Characters troupe styles, how a grog can shift between them, and how easily covenfolk can be advanced in bulk.

title: The Sample Characters (Grog Template Limits)
heading: The Sample Characters
summary: Guidelines for building grogs: no Major Virtues or Flaws, at most three Minor Flaws balanced by an equal number of Minor Virtues, no Story Flaws, and normally no more than one Minor Personality Flaw. Templates should include Covenant Lore and Village Lore.
quotes: Grogs should have no Major Virtues or Flaws, no more than three Minor Flaws balanced by an equal number of Minor Virtues, and no Story Flaws.

title: Magical Alternatives to Covenfolk
heading: Magical Alternatives to Covenfolk
summary: Compares replacing covenfolk with spells, enchanted devices, automata or enchanted parts of the covenant, noting the limits of each: a magus must cast spells and have the Finesse, devices cost time and vis and need a wielder, and people remain more flexible.
quotes: Rego craft magic furthermore depends on the Finesse of the casting magus

title: Rego Craft Magic
heading: Rego Craft Magic
summary: Rules for using Rego to do a craftsman's work: matter cannot be created, a Finesse roll is needed against an Ease Factor at least 3 higher than the mundane craft, failure gives a mess and a botch a hidden flaw, long timespans raise the Ease Factor, and a table gives the minimum Ease Factor by task difficulty.
quotes: +3 for a month's work, +6 for a season's work, or +9 for a year's work
| Trivial           | 0                 | 3                              |
| Almost Impossible | 24+               | 27+                            |

title: New Craft Guidelines: Creo Animal and Rego Animal
heading: New Guidelines
summary: New spell level guidelines for preserving a corpse (Creo Animal) and for manipulating, treating and processing items made of animal products (Rego Animal), with extra magnitudes for greater complexity.
quotes: Level 2: Preserve a corpse from decay.
Level 3: Treat and process items made of animal products.

title: Beasts as Characters
heading: Beasts as Characters
requires: Playing a beast or enchanted animal as a character
summary: Explains how beast characters are built: each species has unbalanced species Virtues and Flaws, exceptional beasts may add balanced individual ones, and normal beasts can improve existing Abilities but only learn new ones if trained, while intelligent beasts advance normally.
quotes: Normal Beasts cannot learn new Abilities unless Trained, but can improve existing Abilities; intelligent beasts can improve as normal.

title: Wealth and Poverty: Rounding and Starting Money
heading: Chapter Five : Wealth & Poverty
summary: Opening rules for covenant finances: round major income and expenditure to whole pounds and ignore small amounts, an autocrat or magus oversees the treasury, and a starting cash reserve can be bought with Build Points.
quotes: Round any major income or expenditure to the nearest pound, and disregard smaller amounts (shillings and pence).
(at the rate of one Build Point per 10 pounds)
